instructions: Using the provided sources, produce a one-page policy brief that summarizes current telehealth adoption trends, the main reimbursement or regulatory constraints, the strongest evidence supporting each major claim, and two unresolved questions that require further investigation.

sources.title: Source 1
sources.content: Health systems report that telehealth use remains above pre-2020 baselines because follow-up visits, behavioral health, and rural access programs continue to rely on virtual care. Patients value reduced travel time and faster appointment availability, but providers note that adoption varies by specialty and patient broadband access.

sources.title: Source 2
sources.content: Several payers have narrowed reimbursement for telehealth after emergency waivers expired. Clinics report that uncertainty around payment parity, cross-state licensing, and documentation rules makes it difficult to treat telehealth capacity as a stable long-term service line.

sources.title: Source 3
sources.content: Policy analysts argue that telehealth works best when paired with clear triage rules: routine monitoring and low-acuity follow-ups can shift online efficiently, while physical examinations, imaging, and complex diagnostics still require in-person care. They caution that utilization gains do not automatically imply lower system-wide costs.

source.title: Source 2 (revised)
source.content: A revised payer survey finds that some large insurers and state Medicaid programs have extended reimbursement parity for selected telehealth services through multi-year policy updates. Clinics still report friction from licensing and compliance rules, but payment uncertainty is less severe than earlier reporting suggested.
